slides.0.title: Three Climate Zones: Atlantic, Continental, Mediterranean
slides.0.subtitle: Level 1 · Portugal's Climate at a Glance
slides.0.points.0.label: Atlantic climate
slides.0.points.0.text: Northwest; wet and cool, producing crisp, high-acid whites
slides.0.points.1.label: Continental climate
slides.0.points.1.text: Central mountains; hot summers, cold winters, large temperature swings, suited to reds

slides.0.points.2.text: South and east; hot, dry and sunny, suited to rich reds
slides.1.title: Atlantic Climate
slides.1.html:
Northwest Portugal is strongly influenced by the Atlantic, giving a mild, humid climate.

📍 Main Regions

  • Minho (Vinho Verde): the most typical Atlantic climate
  • Bairrada: Atlantic-influenced, clay-limestone soils
  • Western Lisboa: coastal areas such as Colares

🌡️ Climate Features

  • Annual rainfall: 1,000–1,500mm (the highest in the country)
  • Cool summers (20–25°C), mild winters (7–12°C)
  • High humidity and a higher risk of fungal disease
  • Suited to: high-acid, crisp, light whites and sparkling wines
slides.2.title: Continental Climate
slides.2.html:
Central Portugal's mountain barriers (Serra da Estrela and others) block the Atlantic's influence, creating a continental climate.

📍 Main Regions

  • Douro: east of the mountains; hot, dry summers and harsh winters
  • Dão: western foothills of Serra da Estrela, with large diurnal range
  • Trás-os-Montes: remote northeast mountains, the most extreme continental climate

🌡️ Climate Features

  • Large annual temperature range: summers up to 35–40°C, winters down to -5°C
  • Annual rainfall: 500–800mm (mostly in winter)
  • A dry summer concentrates the ripening period, favouring colour and sugar accumulation
  • Suited to: structured, deeply coloured, tannic reds
slides.3.title: Mediterranean Climate
slides.3.html:
Southern Portugal (Alentejo, Algarve) and the east are dominated by a Mediterranean climate, hot and dry.

📍 Main Regions

  • Alentejo: vast plains, Portugal's most typical Mediterranean climate
  • Algarve: the far south, with the warmest climate
  • Setúbal Peninsula: moderated by the Atlantic but still warm

🌡️ Climate Features

  • Annual rainfall: 400–600mm (mainly in winter)
  • Long, scorching summers with abundant sunshine; temperatures can exceed 40°C
  • Alentejo receives over 3,000 hours of sunshine a year
  • Suited to: high-alcohol, round and rich reds in a modern style
slides.4.question: Which climate zone does the Minho region, home of Vinho Verde, belong to?
slides.4.explanation: Minho lies right on the Atlantic and is strongly maritime-influenced, giving an Atlantic climate with rainfall up to 1,500mm, which keeps Vinho Verde fresh and high in acidity.
